html:
The Hia-Ced O'odham, the "Sand Dune People", are an O'odham people of the desert between the Ajo Range, the Gila River, the Colorado River and the Gulf of California, on both sides of the border of Arizona and Sonora.

They lived in one of the driest parts of North America, moving between springs and tanks, hunting, gathering desert plants and collecting salt and shellfish on the Gulf. They are kin of the Tohono O'odham and the Akimel O'odham, and lived near the Quechan, the Cocopah and the Seri.

The Gadsden Purchase of 1854 split their land between the United States and Mexico. Disease and settlement scattered them, and they have no federally recognised tribe of their own.
